To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students' experiences of assessment in compulsory education can be described as a living dead culture.

1) students' perceptions of their lecturers are important for students' perceptions of themselves as learners; 2) students' perceptions that they are not able to influence their learning experiences are associated with a negative view of themselves as learners and a lack of engagement with the learning process; and 3) students who have a positive view of themselves as a learner are more likely to have a positive view about their lecturers and to engage with the learning process.
The students' and lecturer's views of the value and usefulness of the Dialogue+ intervention were generally positive.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ways in which students' experiences of assessment in school and university are impacting on students' learner identities, and what this means for their engagement with learning and their ability to succeed.
the impact that assessment has on student identity and the way that this is changing the nature of the student experience.
the ways in which students' and lecturing staff's experiences of assessment in Higher Education are influenced by the assessment practices and cultures that they experienced in compulsory education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zombie students can be awoken and reanimated through the provision of meaningful and relevant assessment and feedback practices.

zombie students are a result of a combination of the way in which schools are preparing young people to become students and the way in which universities are supporting students to be successful in their studies.

the 'undead' can be reanimated and that the 'zombie' metaphor can be used as an analytical tool in educational research to help us to understand the interplay between the assessment of children and young people and the changing nature and expectations of undergraduate students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zombie metaphor is useful for understanding the current situation, but the metaphor also has its limitations.
the zombie metaphor has helped us to understand the nature of assessment and its effects on student identities.

we are trying to create a more inclusive, student-centered approach to assessment and feedback, one which is more responsive to students' needs, and which helps to create a culture of learning in which students are able to take ownership of their learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current assessment system is creating zombies, and that we need to find ways to help students to develop a more positive and proactive approach towards their own learning.
we can no longer assume that students are active learners and that they are aware of the assessment and feedback practices of their universities.

students' and staffs' perceptions of the purpose of assessment are not always in alignment, and that students need to be supported to develop a deeper understanding of the role of assessment within their educational careers.
